title: Sidecar status.json
description: The published integration contract for one pass. A pass execs into the runner container, so the process that wrote this file is routinely not one an integrator can call into — which is why the artifact is the contract and the Ruby classes are private.

schema.description: Read this rather than the exit code when you need to know what produced the file: exit codes are keyed by command and 1 and 2 each mean two different things.

base.description: The git ref, or range, the change set was taken against.

location.description: Which execution location wrote this. Two locations on different core versions is a warning, not a refusal.

load_ms.description: How long the project's config took to load. Recorded rather than guarded: core cannot tell an expensive require from a legitimate one, so a config that boots Rails shows up as the number it is.

slow.description: Absent until the slow tier has actually produced something, so a reader can tell 'not run yet' from 'run and current'.

stale.description: True when the verdict is about a tree that has since moved.

deferred.description: Could not run here: this execution location lacks a resource the sensor needs.

unavailable.description: Could not run at all: the tool itself is not installed. A different problem from deferred, with a different fix.

state.description: error means the tool ran and produced output core could not read — distinct from red, because a crashed linter and a real finding call for different responses.

stale.description: Orthogonal to state. A slow sensor can come back green about a tree that has since moved; the verdict is still green, it is just no longer about the code in front of you.

guidance.description: What to tell whoever this sensor just rejected.

run.description: Lower than considered when a handler rewrites its input and the rewrite names paths that are not on disk — which is how a broken mapping presents.

file.description: Repo-relative. Normalising is the handler's job, since only it knows its tool's path convention.
